# dsh-meter

> A DeepSeek Harness (dsh) Web UI plugin that meters what a session costs
> under DeepSeek's time-of-use pricing: one line in the composer dock with
> the session total, the tariff in force, and the countdown to the next
> change, plus a hover card with a local-time tariff clock, the
> cache/input/output split, and the account balance.

The rate card is written by machine and reviewed by human: a daily job scrapes
both of DeepSeek's pricing pages, rewrites `lib/core.js` from them, regenerates
every artifact, and opens a PR. It never merges one — the invariants CI can
check are structural, and a wrong-but-plausible parse satisfies all of them.

DeepSeek moved to time-of-use billing at 16:00 UTC on 2026-08-16: peak
windows 01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00 UTC, off-peak at half the peak rate.
Each request is priced at the tariff in force when it was **dispatched**,
so a session spanning a boundary is billed correctly on both sides.

Money is computed against both published rate cards (USD for the
international platform, CNY for the mainland one). They are independent
tables, never converted; the account's own `/user/balance` currency
decides which side is shown.

Install: `dsh plugin --profile web add @dshworks/dsh-meter` (npm: `@dshworks/dsh-meter`)

Site: <https://dsh.works/dsh-meter/> — carries a working copy of the tariff
clock (the visitor's own timezone, the live rate card) generated from
`lib/core.js`, so the page cannot state a price the plugin would not.

Pricing feed: <https://dsh.works/dsh-meter/pricing.json> — the same card as
machine-readable JSON for anyone building their own estimator. Static, no
key, no rate limit; both currencies, both tariffs, the UTC schedule, the
retired flat card for repricing history, and the billed-bucket definitions.
Published because no general price aggregator models time-of-use billing:
a schema with one flat price per model cannot express a rate that doubles
for seven hours of every UTC day. A daily job diffs the card against
DeepSeek's own pages and opens an issue on any disagreement.

## Docs

- [README](README.md): what it shows, the rate card, how the money is counted, configuration, limitations
- [README (Chinese)](README.zh.md): the same, in Chinese
- [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md): what each release changed and why
- [SECURITY](SECURITY.md): the one network call, how the API key is resolved, how to turn it off
- [CONTRIBUTING](CONTRIBUTING.md): the generated-bundle rule and what a PR needs

## Source

- [lib/core.js](lib/core.js): the published rate card, the tariff clock, and the pure session-log fold — the single source of both halves
- [lib/balance.js](lib/balance.js): the TTL-cached `GET /user/balance` reader and its error taxonomy
- [lib/index.js](lib/index.js): host plugin — registers the `costMeter` session projection and the `/dsh-meter/balance` route
- [src/ui.js](src/ui.js): browser surface — the composer-dock line, the hover card, and the locale dictionaries
- [scripts/build-client.mjs](scripts/build-client.mjs): inlines core + ui into `lib/client.js`, the bundle dsh serves; `--check` fails when stale
- [scripts/build-site.mjs](scripts/build-site.mjs): inlines core into `docs/index.html`, the GitHub Pages site; renders its schedule strip and rate table from the same exports
- [scripts/build-pricing.mjs](scripts/build-pricing.mjs): renders the card into `docs/pricing.json`, the published feed; `--check` fails when stale
- [scripts/verify-pricing.mjs](scripts/verify-pricing.mjs): scrapes DeepSeek's two pricing pages and diffs them against the card — the daily drift alarm, run outside the test suite
- [scripts/apply-pricing.mjs](scripts/apply-pricing.mjs): writes the scraped rates back into `lib/core.js`, then re-verifies its own output and reverts if that second read disagrees — the card is generated, not typed

## Optional

- [tests/ledger.spec.mjs](tests/ledger.spec.mjs): the fold's contract, including chunk-then-message replacement and boundary-crossing sessions
- [tests/tariff.spec.mjs](tests/tariff.spec.mjs): the rate card and the tariff clock
- [tests/balance.spec.mjs](tests/balance.spec.mjs): the balance reader's caching, coalescing, and failure modes
- [tests/pricing-feed.spec.mjs](tests/pricing-feed.spec.mjs): the published feed's shape — the keys other people's estimators pin against, and the rule that a retired price never appears as a live one
